title: Tesla Roadster
body:
I watched the Tesla livestream, where they unveiled their brand new Roadster. Well, my mind was blown, and I had no words. To be honest, the world is really changing around us.

Sure, some people might argue that we are in no need of a flying car (or at least a car that levitates on its own). I mean sure, they do have a point, but what about the idea that the human race has to keep on building and researching new technology that might not be clear as to what we're actually building towards, but as time moves on, new applications and needs emerge?

So I guess companies like Tesla and SpaceX really push the human race forward.

Technicals:

It seems like this new car is using an electric pump to fill its shell up with air, and then compresses it to high pressure (10,000 psi — Musk's words) and releases it in certain directions. From that presentation, it has around 4 to 6 thrusters on the bottom — to fight weight. There are 4 at the rear end of the car for launch control, and some mini thrusters on the front and back sides of the car for orientation. Some pictures have shown this car having a large shell. I mean, the car can do a 0–60 in about 0.87 seconds, which is completely bonkers.

I mean, my guess is that they have been working on it for the past 7–8 years. Well, the production is starting in 2028. Hopefully, it becomes road legal.

title: Computers
body: Who doesn't like looking at the inside of computers? Among certain nerdy people, the traces, vias, solder joints, and symmetry highlight a perfectionism in these motherboards that is simply out of this world. It is probably the most underrated part of a PC. Developers try to save every bit of bandwidth and optimize the thickness of each trace. There is just so much to consider, and yet all that hard work goes unnoticed.
